candidates.title: U.S. weekly rail traffic shows jump over 2025 levels
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Boosted by a double-digit gain in intermodal volume, U.S. weekly rail traffic showed a sizable increase over 2025 levels for the week ending Oct. 10, 2026. Total volume for the week was 534,256 carloads and intermodal units, an increase of 7.2% over the same week last year. That includes 232,004 carloads, a gain of 3.4%, and 302,252 containers and trailers, up 10.4%. For the year to date, total volume is 20,522,546 carloads and intermodal units, an increase of 3.6% over the first 40 weeks of 2025. The cumulative total of 9,142,597 carloads is up 2.7% from the same period last year, while the 11,379,949 intermodal units represents a 4.4% gain. North American volume for the week, as reported by nine U.S., Canadian, and Mexican railroads, was 725,403 carloads and intermodal units, up 5.9%. candidates.title: BNSF expands security efforts for intermodal shipments
candidates.excerpt: FORT WORTH, Texas — BNSF Railway has announced an expanded partnership with cargo security firm Overhaul to increase supply chain security for customers. The new agreement, which builds on nearly a decade of collaboration, connects BNSF security technology and its police department with the risk intelligence teams of Overhaul. It is intended to identify potential risks earlier, improve coordination, and support secure intermodal freight movement. Gretchen Whitmer announced on Tuesday, Oct. 13. Whitmer also announced the awarding of $65 million for transit projects under the state’s Infrastructure Projects Authority Fund. Though some may look alike, the weathering on each is as unique as the road number assigned to it. There are a variety of factors that influence how prototype equipment weathers, such as how old it is and what type of service it’s in. candidates.title: Opinion: UP-NS still has a long way to go
candidates.excerpt: Trains Turntable: Commentary from Martin J. Oberman Following the burst of rail mergers in the 1990s, the Surface Transportation Board wrote the “new” 2001 merger rules in anticipation of just the kind of merger being proposed by Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. The board said then that it worried about the “end game:” a further reduction in the number of Class I railroads, “perhaps to the point where only two major railroads remain in the U.S. and Canada,” with massive market power. To guard against that outcome, the board raised the bar, saying merger applicants should bear a heavier burden to prove that a merger is in the public interest. The board promised “a more skeptical, ‘show me’ attitude toward claims of merger benefits.” And it added a crucial test: whether the claimed benefits could be achieved “by means other than the proposed consolidation,” such as interline partnerships, thus avoiding the anti-competitive risks that would come with further mergers. candidates.title: One injured in Norfolk Southern derailment in North Carolina
candidates.excerpt: MORGANTON, N.C. — One injury was reported after a Norfolk Southern train derailed this afternoon, WSOC-TV reports. The derailment occurred about 3:30 p.m. While the station reports a locomotive and five cars were involved, a second locomotive appears visible in a Facebook image posted by volunteer response group Burke Rescue Inc. The injured party was transported to a hospital with injuries described as minor. No hazardous materials were spilled in the incident. U.S. Route 70 was expected to be closed at the derailment scene for 24 hours, according to a Facebook post from Morganton Public Safety. Morganton is on the NS Asheville District, about 60 miles east of Asheville, N.C., and 78 miles west of Salisbury. — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com. candidates.excerpt: Direwolf cyber risk under the radar? Take care, no target is too small Cyber extortion group ‘n0n’ has named 38 organisations across the global shipping and ports sector on its dark-web leak site, raising concerns that data may have been stolen. Cybersecurity firm SOCRadar reported yesterday n0n published the listings in a single batch on 12 October. They included container terminals, shipping lines, port IT providers, and logistics businesses across 18 countries. None of the maritime organisations named had publicly confirmed a breach at the time of writing. South Korea accounted for 12 listings, including Busan terminal operators BNCT and Pusan Newport Co. The list included Brazilian port operators Santos Brasil, Portonave, and Superterminais; Singapore-based carrier ONE; China’s CULines; Taiwan’s TS Lines; Spain’s TTI Algeciras; and Morocco’s Eurogate Tanger. candidates.title: Update: Singapore confirms container ship sunk in Hormuz amid fresh Iran attacks
candidates.excerpt: UKMTO has issued four new warnings of separate attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, reporting strikes on a tanker and three container ships on 13 October. The vessels were each hit by unknown projectiles and were not identified in the warning notices, but Vanguard Tech has identified the container ships as GFS Pride, GFS Giselle, and Al Saadiyat and the tanker as Alfonso. The four attacks bring UKMTO’s tally of warnings to 24 for the month of October to date, as well as three advisories. Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) confirmed that Singapore-flagged GFS Pride has sunk since a projectile strike caused damage and a fire onboard. All 21 crew were safely evacuated, it added. Vanguard Tech said GFS Giselle suffered minor damage after being struck during its inbound transit before continuing on its way with no injuries reported; MPA confirmed the 22 crew were safe and that the ship has arrived at safe anchorage despite sustaining hull damage. candidates.excerpt: Moody’s: life insurers increasingly rely on RNFs US life insurers are increasingly using rated note feeders (RNFs) to gain exposure to private credit markets, according to a report by Moody’s Ratings. Alongside the potential for diversification and enhanced yields, RNFs are seen as a capital efficient way of accessing private strategies such as direct lending, infrastructure, asset-based finance, and commercial real estate. Moody’s estimates that 35 per cent of US life insurance investments go towards private credit. Read more: Private credit boom pushes fund finance market past $1tn Among the fastest-growing fund finance vehicles, RNFs are structured as a special purpose vehicle which issues one or multiple classes of tranched debt, typically senior and junior notes, alongside an unrated equity tranche.
